- Model tends to overestimate prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Overshoots occur after sharp price spikes (e.g., 79.16 → 82.30 or 79.68 → 81.87), leading to overcorrection in subsequent days.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized; model fails to smoothly decay toward historical averages after peaks.
- Forecast lags behind true price movements by 1–3 days, particularly in the middle to late horizon (days 15–30).
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher values in the 20–30 day forecast window, especially when recent history shows downward momentum.
- When true price drops sharply (e.g., 82.31 → 80.17), model fails to adjust downward and remains elevated for 2–4 days.
- Model overreacts to short-term volatility; ignores underlying trend persistence in favor of noise-driven adjustments.
